data.label: Flood
data.description: Flood events with daily satellite rainfall over each event box and the NISAR soil moisture passes over the same box, and a forecast of the flood within the next 3 days (danger when the probability reaches the model threshold), from the team notebook flood_disaster.ipynb.

target.label: Flood within the next 3 days
target.definition: 1 if the reported flood period (in_flood_period) covers at least one of the next 3 calendar days, else 0; unknown (null) when any of those days is outside the data.

dataset.description: Flood events with daily satellite rainfall over each event box (GPM IMERG) and the NISAR soil moisture passes over the same box, from 7 days (rain) / 12 days (soil) before the reported flood period to its end.

columns.rain_box_mm: Rain averaged over the event box, mm/day (GPM IMERG Late Run V07; cells weighted by their area inside the box)
columns.rain_wettest_cell_mm: Rain in the wettest 0.1-degree (~10 km) IMERG cell of the box that day, mm/day
columns.cells_with_data: Number of IMERG cells in the box with a value that day
columns.in_flood_period: true on the days of the reported flood period (flood_start..flood_end), false on the 7 days of lead-up rain before it

columns.file: Source GeoTIFF of the pass (not copied; 200 m EASE-Grid 2.0, 4 bands)
columns.date: UTC date of the pass, YYYY-MM-DD
columns.utc_time: UTC time of the pass, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
columns.local_time: Local time of the pass, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
columns.phase: before / onset / during / receding / after / unclear, relative to the flood timeline
columns.in_reported_flood_period: true if the pass falls in the reported flood period
columns.cells_in_box: Number of 200 m cells in the event box
columns.cells_with_soil_moisture: Cells with a soil moisture value (open water, towns, snow and heavy rain are empty)
columns.coverage_pct: % of the box with a value
columns.mean_sm: Box mean soil moisture, m3/m3 (all values)
columns.p10_sm: 10th percentile of soil moisture in the box, m3/m3
columns.p90_sm: 90th percentile of soil moisture in the box, m3/m3
columns.mean_sm_recommended_only: Box mean of "recommended" retrievals only (dense vegetation left out), m3/m3; the value the flood model uses
columns.phase_reason: Why the pass got its phase label

datasets.name: GPM IMERG Late Run, daily, V07 (GPM_3IMERGDL.07)
datasets.citation: Huffman, G.J., Stocker, E.F., Bolvin, D.T., Nelkin, E.J., Tan, J. (2024). GPM IMERG Late Precipitation L3 1 day 0.1 degree x 0.1 degree V07, edited by A. Savtchenko. Greenbelt, MD: Goddard Earth Sciences Data and Information Services Center (GES DISC). doi:10.5067/GPM/IMERGDL/DAY/07.

datasets.name: NISAR L3 SME2 soil moisture, provisional, version 1
datasets.citation: NISAR L3 SME2 Soil Moisture, Provisional, Version 1 (NASA/JPL-Caltech & ISRO), via the Alaska Satellite Facility DAAC. doi:10.5067/NIL3SME2-P1. Product guide: https://nisar-docs.asf.alaska.edu/sme2/

notes: Days are UTC days: (00:00 to 24:00 UTC), not local days.

The rain is a satellite estimate: The Late Run is available about a day after the rain, but it is not corrected with rain gauges. NASA's gauge-corrected Final Run comes out about 3.5 months later. In October 2026 it only went up to September 2025, so none of these events have it yet.
River floods are fed by rain upstream: For Mozambique, Pakistan, Patna and Bhagalpur, much of the water came from rain upstream, outside the box. The box rain shows only the local part.
Nepal (Trishuli): was caused by a glacier/rock collapse, not by rain.

Empty cells (no value): NASA leaves out open water, rivers and lakes, towns, snow and frozen ground, and areas with excessive rain. Flooded land is therefore often empty during a flood. Soil moisture is most useful before the flood.

Coverage differs between tracks: Each track sees a different part of the box, so its average covers different ground. Compare passes of the same track (one line in the chart). The chart labels show how much of the box each pass covers.
Dense vegetation: Values under dense forest or tall crops are marked "not recommended" by NASA. They're kept in soil_moisture, but mean_sm_recommended_only in the CSV leaves them out.
Provisional: NASA says this product is only partly checked so far ("partially validated"), and its accuracy goal is ±0.06 m³/m³ where vegetation is not dense.
Days are UTC in the file names: Local times and labels are in the CSV.
